panel: theme-climate-r1 blind panel 5 (3 fresh Opus + 1 Argon), 2026-10-23
rule: a major counts only if at least 2 of the 4 judges raise the same problem; pick = candidate with 0 counted majors, majority vote among those (Opus majority on ties)
prompt:
# Blind review panel — dungeon chipset pieces

You are one independent judge. Do not edit or create any files; only open the PNG boards below with the Read tool
(they are large; read each one fully). No other context is needed.

Each board is one item for an OPRN 16px RPG chipset in 3/4 top-down view (RPG Maker style: tops are visible planes, fronts below them,
no side faces, light from top-left). At the top of the board are REFERENCE crops from the existing "Beodeul" chipset (the quality
bar) at 1x and 3x and an RPG Maker person for scale. Below are anonymous candidates labelled X and Y for the same item: the piece at 1x and
3x, its parts, a small scene at 1x and 2x (animated items show all frames side by side), and extras (tile mosaics / test maps) for
floors, walls and autotiles.

Judge each candidate against these criteria:
1. reads correctly in 3/4 top-down at 1x (top planes visible, fronts below, no side/isometric faces, sits on the floor with contact);
2. sits in the same game as the Beodeul reference (palette harmony, texture density, number of shading steps, no toy/flat/clip-art look,
   no black ink outlines);
3. seamless joins: floors/walls/autotiles show no visible 16px repeat or seams; multi-cell objects join without cuts;
4. reads as its stated purpose and as its theme (the board title says what it is).

A MAJOR problem = something that would make you refuse to ship it (misreads at 1x, wrong view, clearly below the reference's quality,
visible seams/grid, does not read as the item). A MINOR problem = worth polishing but shippable.

Reply with ONLY a JSON object, no prose before or after:
{"<board file name without .png>": {"X": {"majors": [{"problem": "...", "where": "..."}], "minors": [{"problem": "...", "where": "..."}]},
                                    "Y": {"majors": [...], "minors": [...]},
                                    "pick": "X" or "Y", "why": "one sentence"}, ...}

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_idol.note: A1 helmet-on-bog major by one judge only

minors.problem: The curved sagging plank detail on the intact end piece reads slightly like a chest latch at 1x

majors.problem: Planks are broken into noisy short brick-like segments with vertical posts cutting through the top surface, failing to match the horizontal plank rhythm of the reference boardwalk
majors.where: Y part 1 and scene join with reference boardwalk

minors.problem: Floating diagonal wood fragments in the broken variant look scattered and disconnected on the water

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_boardwalk.why: X matches the reference boardwalk's horizontal plank width, palette, and join lines cleanly while clearly reading as intact and broken boardwalk ends.

minors.problem: Silhouette is slightly boxy and symmetrical, and the bottom water-contact ripple line is a bit straight
minors.where: X piece outer silhouette and bottom row

majors.problem: Reads as a small knight helmet or turret sitting on a bright tan mud island rather than a 2x2 stone idol head half-sunk in a bog, and the tan mound clashes with the dark swamp water
majors.where: Y piece whole object and lower mud base in scene

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_idol.why: X clearly reads at 1x as a mossy carved stone idol head partially submerged in swamp water, whereas Y looks like a small helmet on a floating dirt patch.

majors.problem: Pads curl upward with heavy vertical volume like upright cabbages or bushes rather than flat floating lily pads on the water plane
majors.where: X part 1 and part 2 pad bodies

minors.problem: Both variants include a prominent bright flower, making repeated placement in the scene look uniform and busy
Single-pixel yellow-green highlights and scattered duckweed dots have slightly high contrast against the dark water
minors.where: Y part 1 and part 2 pad rims and surrounding water

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_lily.why: Y sits flat on the water surface in 3/4 view with clear notched lily-pad silhouettes and natural variety between the flowering and non-flowering variants.

minors.problem: Hanging moss curtains fall in slightly stiff vertical columns at 1x
minors.where: X piece left and right hanging moss

majors.problem: High-contrast grey bark and speckled yellow-green pixels create severe pixel noise at 1x and clash with the warm brown reference dead tree in the same scene

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_moss.why: X matches the reference dead-tree bark palette and shading while clearly reading as draped hanging moss over dead branches at 1x.

majors.problem: Saturated cyan palette clashes with the warm Beodeul swamp palette, and the solid reflection disc makes it read like a rigid glass marker or pin rather than a floating flame
majors.where: X parts 1..3 orb and lower reflection disc

minors.problem: Animation frames show very little motion at 1x
Flame silhouette in the middle frame is slightly diamond-symmetric and lacks a subtle glow on the water below

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_wisp.why: Y harmonizes with the reference lantern's warm spectral glow and reads clearly as a flickering floating will-o'-wisp across its three animation frames.

minors.problem: the broken-end cell shows a flat grey-blue backdrop through the gap. It reads as a cutout rather than swamp water and clashes with the dark green bog in the scene
the support post/rail on the front edge reads a little like a table apron and not much like pilings
the splintered planks and diagonal broken boards are busier and noisier than the reference's calm plank texture. At 1x the end looks messy
the grey-blue gap shows through the broken section the same way as in X

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_boardwalk.why: X keeps the plank rhythm and value range of the Beodeul deck and reads more cleanly as a boardwalk end at 1x. Y's splintering turns into noise.

minors.problem: the face is mostly horizontal grey bands with a soft lumpy outline. At 1x it reads more as a mossy boulder than a carved idol head
the waterline contact is a pale grey rim and not dark bog, so the head looks set on top of the water rather than half sunk

majors.problem: it sits on a large pale olive mud mound that does not match the dark bog water around it and looks like a pasted island. It also does not read as 'half sunk in bog'

minors.problem: the head is small inside the 2x2 footprint and the spiky crown is noisy at 1x

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_idol.why: X reads as a stone mass sunk directly into the water with a coherent value range, while Y's bright mud island clashes with the bog.

minors.problem: the pads are dense, bright lime clumps with a lot of volume. They read a bit like floating shrubs, not flat pads on water
the saturation runs slightly above the reference's muted swamp water
the flat ring outlines with notches read slightly diagrammatic and less textured than the reference
the small specks around the pads add scattered noise

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_lily.why: Y reads as flat lily pads lying on the water surface in top-down view and blends with the swamp water, while X looks like floating bushes.

minors.problem: the hanging moss is pale grey-green streaks to one side and could read as dripping paint at 1x
the trunk base needs a slightly stronger ground contact shadow

majors.problem: the moss mass is so dense and yellow-green that it hides the dead branches. At 1x it reads as a small leafy/weeping tree, not dead branches with hanging moss

minors.problem: the moss is speckled with light dots, which adds noise compared with the reference's clean bark shading

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_moss.why: X keeps the bare dead-trunk silhouette of the reference tree with moss hanging off it, so it reads as its purpose at 1x.

majors.problem: it is a large, saturated cyan balloon with a ground glow puddle. It reads as a toy balloon or water drop, and its look (palette and clip-art shine) does not belong with the muted Beodeul set

minors.problem: the frame-to-frame change is small; the bob is weak
it is very small at 1x and barely reads as more than a spark. A soft glow halo would help
the yellow-green flame is close in hue to the lamp reference but could use one more shading step

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_wisp.why: Y reads as a small flickering marsh flame in a palette that matches the reference lamp. X looks like a cyan toy balloon.

minors.problem: The broken end reads more like a gap with a cross-beam than splintered planks. The water showing through is flat grey-blue, not the swamp water colour.
The support-post fronts look a little like furniture legs (table-like rail).
The diagonal fallen plank is busy and noisy at 1x, so the broken end is harder to read.
The water gap is a flat grey hole that doesn't match the swamp water tile.

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_boardwalk.why: Y's tilted, splintered plank reads more clearly as a broken boardwalk end, and its wood texture matches the reference deck equally well.

majors.problem: At 1x it reads as a grey helmet or robot head sitting on top of the bog, not half sunk. There is no waterline or bog occlusion.

minors.problem: The stone is fairly uniform light grey with few moss patches, so it looks a bit clean for a swamp.
The head is small for 2x2, and the spiky crown reads a bit like a castle turret at 1x.
The yellow-ochre mud mound is lighter than the surrounding bog water and grass palette.

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_idol.why: Y's mud mound gives the head contact and a half-sunk feel, while X floats on the bog like a helmet.

majors.problem: The pads are drawn as bushy, leafy heaps rather than flat floating discs, so at 1x they read as shrubs on the water.

minors.problem: Light lime highlights are brighter than the reference swamp greens.
The pads are small and sparse, so the 'cluster' reads a little thin at 1x.
The tiny light-blue flecks around the pads look like noise.

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_lily.why: Y's flat round pads with notches read correctly as lily pads lying on the water in 3/4 view.

minors.problem: There are few branches, so it reads more as a stump with moss curtains than as dead branches.

majors.problem: The upper half is a dense yellow-green moss blob that hides the branches, so at 1x it reads as a bushy small tree or broom rather than dead branches with hanging moss.

minors.problem: The blue-grey speckles in the moss clash with the reference palette.

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_moss.why: X keeps the dead-wood silhouette consistent with the reference stilt tree, with moss clearly hanging from it.

majors.problem: The saturated cyan glossy orbs with a cyan ground ring look like clip-art balloons or gems. They are off-palette against the muted swamp and don't read as a ghostly light.

minors.problem: The frames differ only slightly, so the animation is barely visible at 1x.

theme-climate-r1__tc.sw_wisp.why: Y's pale yellow-green flickering flame with sparks reads as a will-o-wisp and fits the muted swamp palette, while X looks like cyan clip-art orbs.

minors.problem: the broken end shows dark gray where water should be, so at 1x it reads more like a gap than like water under the planks

minors.problem: the speckled texture is denser and noisier than the clean plank grain in the reference
